quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.
Take the right-of-way.
Drive normally.
Drive away quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you must slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light works the same way as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop. Let all other traffic go first before you move.

questions.question: A sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph" means:

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should only reduce your speed to 35 mph in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: When you see a "Reduced speed" sign with a speed limit on it, that speed limit applies right away at that sign.

questions.question: You must be extra careful when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: The person is deaf.
The person is a police officer.
The person is blind.
The person has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: The person is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane shows that a pedestrian is blind. You must slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: Taking drugs while drinking alcohol:

options.text: Increases the chance of a crash.
Is just as safe as drinking alcohol alone.
Makes alcohol's effect on your driving smaller.
Does not affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the chance of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (legal or illegal) can hurt your ability to drive safely. Mixing drugs with alcohol makes things much more dangerous and greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: When you leave a driveway to enter the street, you must:

options.text: Drive slowly so other vehicles and pedestrians can move out of your way.
Honk your horn so other vehicles and pedestrians know to give you space.
Stop and only move when no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
You can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and only move when no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Always stop before you drive onto the street from a driveway. Wait until all pedestrians and vehicles have passed. It is against the law not to stop.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the guard says something else.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow rules that would apply if no children were there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
questions.explanation: Always follow directions from a crossing guard or police officer in a school zone. Drive slowly and carefully in school zones.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive no faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. You must use headlights when you can only see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep driving at your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Let pedestrians cross first.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: You can turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When you turn, you must let pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection go first.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Four lanes of traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Intersection ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is moving in both directions ahead.

questions.question: You are stopped in a line of vehicles at a stop sign. After the vehicles ahead pass through and there is no other traffic, you:

options.text: May go through the intersection without stopping again.
Must stop at the stop sign or stop line before going forward.
May slowly roll past the stop sign.
May follow the vehicle ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop at the stop sign or stop line before going forward.
questions.explanation: You must always make a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Do not skip this stop just because other vehicles are around you.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the road onto the shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed without braking hard. Then carefully turn back onto the road. Watch for other vehicles nearby.

questions.question: Drugs can affect your ability to drive safely:

options.text: Only if they are not prescribed by a doctor.
Only when taken with alcohol.
Only when driving at night.
Even if prescribed by a doctor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if prescribed by a doctor.
questions.explanation: Many medicines can affect your driving ability. Ask your doctor about side effects before starting any medication.

questions.question: An arrow painted on the road means:

options.text: You may make the movement shown by the arrow if you want to.
You must make the movement shown by the arrow only if traffic lights are broken.
You must always stop before making the movement shown by the arrow.
You must make the movement shown by the arrow while following traffic signal directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must make the movement shown by the arrow while following traffic signal directions.
questions.explanation: An arrow on the road tells you what direction to go. Follow any traffic signals before moving in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: A "No stopping" sign means you may stop only if:

options.text: Long enough to unload packages.
Needed to avoid a crash with another vehicle.
To let passengers out.
For less than five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needed to avoid a crash with another vehicle.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, obey a police officer, or prevent a crash.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive at the posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive close behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed when it rains. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see well, pull over and stop until it clears.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Lowers your blood alcohol level.
Removes the effect of the alcohol.
Does not change your blood alcohol level.
Raises your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee will not lower your blood alcohol level. It may keep you awake, but it cannot make you sober.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Use your four-way flashers.
Use your parking lights.
Not turn on any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk and on overcast days. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of oncoming traffic and within 500 feet of traffic ahead. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: You may cross a dashed white line:

options.text: At any time.
Only during the day.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You may cross them to change lanes when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If you are in an accident and another person is injured, what should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless you must. Moving them the wrong way can make a minor injury worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, press directly on the wound to stop the blood.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, what should you do?

options.text: Look for turning vehicles before crossing a street.
Never run alongside or across a street.
Walk on the left side of the street, facing traffic.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not run alongside or across a street. Walk on the left side of the street facing oncoming traffic. Always look for turning vehicles before you cross a street.

questions.question: What does a steady green light mean?

options.text: You must slow down and get ready to stop.
You must stop and check for oncoming traffic before going.
You can drive through the intersection if the road is clear.
You cannot turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can drive through the intersection if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if the road is clear. You can also turn right or left on a steady green light unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, let other vehicles and pedestrians go first.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
Keep driving at the same speed.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk your horn to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not drive in someone else's blind spot. Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed for drivers going in both directions.
Passing is not allowed.
Passing is allowed if you are at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during daylight only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines show that traffic on the other side is moving the opposite direction. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass in either direction.

questions.question: What affects how much space you need to cross traffic?

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
The presence of a stop sign.
Using your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.
Busy sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a pedestrian crossing. Watch for people entering a crosswalk or crossing your path. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: If you are in an accident and oncoming traffic cannot see the scene, what should you do?

options.text: Have someone warn approaching traffic.
Let oncoming traffic watch out for themselves.
Let the police handle everything.
Assume other drivers heard the crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have someone warn approaching traffic.
questions.explanation: If the accident scene is not visible to oncoming traffic, warn approaching drivers to prevent more crashes. Keep a flashlight and flares in your vehicle for emergencies.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Make sure your tires are filled to the correct pressure.
Slow down when driving in the rain.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, make sure your tires have good tread and are filled to the correct pressure. Slow down when driving in the rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at higher speeds.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop?

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: The condition of the road greatly affects your ability to stop. Slow down when roads are poor so you can control your vehicle. Driving too fast on slippery roads makes it hard to stop and puts you at risk.
